precepts.text: When the noblest offspring of the Egyptians was destroyed in one moment, they who would believe nothing by reason of the enchantments acknowledged this people to be the sons of God.
precepts.point: It is in our DNA: anything we do we excel at, while being held back; that is why reading was a crime for a slave and why every revolt began with slaves who read.

note.label: The Superiority of the Chosen People

precepts.why:
In 1 Samuel 4 the Philistines heard the great shout “in the camp of the Hebrews”, and that is us. The ark of the covenant had come into our possession, and we rejoiced. They said, “Woe unto us! who shall deliver us out of the hand of these mighty Gods? these are the Gods that smote the Egyptians with all the plagues in the wilderness.” The Philistines called us gods, mighty Gods. Wisdom of Solomon 18 shows the Egyptians coming to the same place.

“So they all together had innumerable dead with one kind of death; neither were the living sufficient to bury them: for in one moment the noblest offspring of them was destroyed.” That is when Christ came down and killed all the firstborn of the Egyptians, all the Egyptians’ babies.

“For whereas they would not believe any thing by reason of the enchantments.” The Egyptians did not believe anything we had to say about being God’s people, by reason of their witches. “Upon the destruction of the firstborn, they acknowledged this people to be the sons of God.” After God gave them hell, they realized: these are the sons of God, these are God’s children.

The heathen have always known it. Don’t think for one second these Asians don’t understand it today; that is why they dumb us down on purpose. It is in our DNA: anything we do we excel at, while being held back at the same time. Why do you think it was a law for us not to read, and they would kill those that did know how to read? Because every time we read we start learning who we are, and then we start rising up. Many slave revolts took place where the slaves started reading and rose up and killed their masters, and they hid all of it. We are on another level in our DNA, and the nations acknowledge us to be the sons of God.

precepts.text: The Lord instructed Moses to hew two tables of stone like unto the first, make an ark of wood, and put in it the tables the Lord would write on.
precepts.point: So what is the ark of the covenant, and what does it contain? The Lord told Moses to hew two tables of stone like the first ones he broke, and the Lord rewrote the ten commandments on them with his own finger, and Moses put the tables in the ark. The ark of the covenant contained the commandments that God wrote.

note.label: 1 Samuel 4: The Ark of God Is Taken

precepts.why:
The elders of Israel asked the right question: “Wherefore hath the Lord smitten us to day before the Philistines?” But instead of examining the nation, they had an idea: “Let us fetch the ark of the covenant of the Lord out of Shiloh unto us, that, when it cometh among us, it may save us out of the hand of our enemies.”

So what is the ark of the covenant, and what does it contain? “Hew thee two tables of stone like unto the first, and come up unto me into the mount, and make thee an ark of wood. And I will write on the tables the words that were in the first tables which thou brakest, and thou shalt put them in the ark.” The ark was made to hold the tables the Lord would write on.

precepts.text: Moses broke the first tables when he came down from the mount and saw the people dancing before the golden calf they had made from their gold earrings.
precepts.point: So what is the ark of the covenant, and what does it contain? The Lord told Moses to hew two tables of stone like the first ones he broke, and the Lord rewrote the ten commandments on them with his own finger, and Moses put the tables in the ark. The ark of the covenant contained the commandments that God wrote.

note.label: 1 Samuel 4: The Ark of God Is Taken

precepts.why:
The first tables were broken. Moses came down, and “as soon as he came nigh unto the camp, that he saw the calf, and the dancing: and Moses’ anger waxed hot, and he cast the tables out of his hands, and brake them beneath the mount.” The people were dancing before the golden calf they had made from their gold earrings.

That is why the Lord told Moses to hew two tables of stone like the first ones he broke, and the Lord rewrote the ten commandments on them with his own finger.

precepts.text: Moses made an ark of shittim wood, the Lord wrote on the tables the ten commandments he spake out of the midst of the fire, and Moses put the tables in the ark, and there they be.
precepts.point: So what is the ark of the covenant, and what does it contain? The Lord told Moses to hew two tables of stone like the first ones he broke, and the Lord rewrote the ten commandments on them with his own finger, and Moses put the tables in the ark. The ark of the covenant contained the commandments that God wrote.

note.label: 1 Samuel 4: The Ark of God Is Taken

precepts.why:
“And I made an ark of shittim wood, and hewed two tables of stone like unto the first.” “And he wrote on the tables, according to the first writing, the ten commandments, which the Lord spake unto you in the mount out of the midst of the fire.” Then Moses “put the tables in the ark which I had made; and there they be, as the Lord commanded me.” The ark of the covenant contained the commandments that God wrote.

The law is spiritual, and the law has literal spiritual power; the commandments have always been our source of power as a nation. The church teaches that the laws are done away with, but watch in these chapters how seriously the Lord regarded the ark that contained his commandments.

When “the ark of the covenant of the Lord came into the camp, all Israel shouted with a great shout, so that the earth rang again.” The two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with it. That is how excited and ecstatic Israel was to have the ark among them; they felt their enemies could not destroy them now.

But watch why the ark did not have the effect Israel expected in this battle: there were still Israelites in the midst of idolatry with idols among them, and until those idols were put away we could not be delivered from our enemies. That is the lesson Samuel drives home in chapter 7.

precepts.text: The Most High destroyed many kings for Israel's sake; Pharaoh and all his power is the most popular account, and the Philistines knew it.
precepts.point: Still the Philistines rallied: be strong, and quit yourselves like men, O ye Philistines, that ye be not servants unto the Hebrews, as they have been to you. They remembered serving Israel in the days of the Judges and refused to be slaves again, so they got ready to fight.

note.label: 1 Samuel 4: The Ark of God Is Taken

precepts.why:
“Many kings have I destroyed for their sakes; Pharaoh with his servants and all his power have I smitten down.” The Most High destroyed many kings for Israel's sake. Pharaoh and all his power is the most popular account, and the Philistines knew it.

“And the Philistines were afraid, for they said, God is come into the camp.” They had never had to battle Israel with the ark of the covenant in the camp. They cried, “who shall deliver us out of the hand of these mighty Gods? these are the Gods that smote the Egyptians with all the plagues in the wilderness.” The nations knew what the Most High did to Egypt. It was known throughout the earth, and to this day real history about what the Hebrews and their God did to the Egyptians is still taught on the other side of the earth. With the ark of the commandments among us, the nations understood they were dealing with something above a regular people.

Everything our people try to glory in about Kemet, the Lord smote down. The ten plagues humiliated ten plus different gods that the Egyptians served, all their power, all their magicians and wizards. Come out of that Kemet movement; the Lord destroyed it and said Egypt would not rise again as a power in the earth.

Still the Philistines rallied: “Be strong, and quit yourselves like men, O ye Philistines, that ye be not servants unto the Hebrews, as they have been to you.” They remembered serving Israel in the days of the Judges and refused to be slaves again, so they got ready to fight.

precepts.point: When it says 'according to the will of God and our Father,' God refers to Christ (who is called God in Hebrews 1:8) and Father refers to the Most High.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

precepts.why:
The Philistines cried, “Woe unto us! who shall deliver us out of the hand of these mighty Gods? these are the Gods that smote the Egyptians with all the plagues in the wilderness.”

Even the Philistines spoke of mighty Gods, more than one, who smote the Egyptians. That fits “God and our Father”: Christ, who is called God, and the Most High his Father. It is the will of both that Christ gave himself to deliver us from this present evil world.

points: Eli was ninety and eight years old and his eyes were dim, and when the messenger told him Israel fled, the slaughter was great, thy two sons are dead, and the ark of God is taken, at the mention of the ark of God he fell from off the seat backward by the side of the gate, and his neck brake, and he died, for he was an old man, and heavy. The shock of the ark being taken is what took him off that seat.
He had judged Israel forty years, and his death was ultimately part of the judgment for how he dealt with his sons, in that he did not correct them as he should have.

points: Phinehas' wife was with child, near to be delivered, and when she heard the tidings that the ark of God was taken and that her father in law and her husband were dead, she bowed herself and travailed, giving birth before her time under all that misfortune.

note.label: 1 Samuel 4: The Ark of God Is Taken

points: Dying, she named the child Ichabod, saying, The glory is departed from Israel: for the ark of God is taken. Remember what the ark contained, the commandments; with the ark gone, she said the glory of Israel was gone. It was a very sad time for the nation of Israel: thirty thousand mighty men lost, Eli dead, and the ark in the hands of the Philistines.
